gAction.scope: Defines the signed half-angle update of the two selected real rows, leaving other rows unchanged. A single column gives the site-amplitude rule. The definition gives no test from probabilities, propagation bound or scheduling optimum.

gSplit.scope: For any two signed real numbers, the cosine and sine of half the split angle, multiplied by their Euclidean pair norm, reproduce the two numbers. This is a two-coordinate existence ingredient.

gPairSq.scope: The square of the real pair norm is the sum of the two squared entries. No graph or measurement identification is part of this equality.

gFixed.scope: A basis column whose index is outside the two selected indices equals the corresponding identity column in every row.

gStep.scope: The frozen snapshot marks this record Partial route with status legacy_source_semantic_debt. Its declaration text records two numerical indices whose second is one above the first and one real angle. This supports only the path-edge convention. The separate rotation and elimination declarations provide its local mathematical ingredients; the record gives no optimality result.

gPivot.scope: For any real pair the specified elimination angle takes it to its nonnegative norm in the first position and zero in the second. Reorientation of endpoints and use in tree schedules are further deductions.

gUndo.scope: A list of adjacent steps is inverted on any real rectangular array by reversing the list and negating its angles. This is an exact replay identity for that list, independent of any count lower bound.

gOrth.scope: A plane matrix on distinct indices is orthogonal. This supplies exact norm preservation on each edge. It does not assert that a whole sphere is reachable within a specified depth.

gInverse.scope: The rotation of any two distinct real rows is undone by the negative angle on those rows. It applies to a tree edge with either fixed endpoint order, without implying a schedule theorem.
